title: Python Function Parameters and Arguments
learningObjectives: Explain the behavior of python function parameters and arguments.
Write and call functions using appropriate parameter forms.
Predict argument binding, scope and return behavior.
Choose suitable function constructs for a practical task.
Apply readable function design and avoid common pitfalls.

understand.concept: Parameters are names in a function definition; arguments are the values supplied when the function is called. Positional arguments are matched to parameters by position. A function can have multiple parameters, and each required parameter must receive a corresponding argument unless it has a default.
understand.whyItMatters: Parameters allow one function to work with different input values instead of hard-coding data.
understand.analogy: Parameters are empty labeled slots in a form; arguments are the actual values entered into those slots.
understand.analogyLimit: Argument binding rules include positional-only, keyword-only and variadic forms; this lesson focuses on basic positional and keyword calls.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Parameters in a definition

Write parameter names inside the function's parentheses.

## 2. Arguments in a call

Supply argument values when calling the function. Positional arguments match parameters from left to right.

## 3. Multiple inputs

A function can accept several parameters and use each value in its body.
